I will play Devil's Advocate here, as there are many different flavors of nihilism and a person may hold only one or several of the varying flavors of it. Existential and Moral Nihilism are the most routinely targeted, in the case of existential nihilism: "Why do you believe life is meaningless or has no value" or in the case of moral nihilism "How can you not see killing someone is worse than handing them a gift"-------The understanding being that moral nihilists don't see one action as preferable to another in a 'moral' context, actions just 'are', there is no good or evil about it. Moral nihilists may believe killing someone has a potentially net-negative benefit (for whatever reason) but that doesn't have to do with morals since they'd argue that morals are abstract rules made up by people.

Arguably, nihilism is one of the more poorly understood philosophical doctrines that usually just gets ham-fisted into witty quips about "believing in nothing". I will fully admit that there are more 'learned' individuals who are far better at explaining facets of nihilism than I can. Nonetheless, I'd argue that a better way to approach nihilism is not to think "nihilists believe in nothing", but to think that "nihilists believe everything ever told to them is a lie".

Imagine your grandfather gave you a tool box. In this toolbox are all the tools that he believes you'll need to navigate through life. Imagine the tools themselves as physical objects that represent abstract concepts, like morals or ideologies or even different philosophies or even just everything you've ever been told (or even reality itself). Some of the more enterprising humans see morals as a hammer to beat others down with, others may see their morals as a hand planer or a compass. Now apply that thinking to everything in the toolbox-- IMO a fairly accurate representation as to what most people carry around with them-- at least conceptually.

What nihilists do, is take that toolbox and dump it on the ground. Now it is perfectly valid to walk around with an empty toolbox if you want and some people do. Other people start putting tools back in the box or create new tools as they need them. Maybe that 'screw driver' their grandfather handed them had the blunt end of a hammer on the end instead of something that turns screws, maybe that pair of pliers they received was entirely made of rubber so they couldn't grip anything.

Now morals/spirituality/religion can be argued to issue these toolboxes as 'kits'. I will use Catholics as an example (not hating on Catholics, but I think its a good example to use given that the Catholic Church is very 'top-down' heavy if you know what I mean). Now imagine when a catholic baby is born the couple goes to the priest and says here 'look at my baby'. The priest goes 'oh, I know exactly what to do with this' and hands the couple an extra toolbox (just like the one they received when they were children). Now the Catholic toolbox has a very specific set of tools inside, tools that are arguably intended to keep the flock returning to the Church for spiritual reasons from one angle and wealth/power (at least for the upper echelons of the Church) on another angle. These kinds of 'kit' toolboxes are not restricted to Catholicism alone and there are many other denominations or religions (or even just the moral beliefs of parents themselves) that provide similar kits. Where you fall on whether a kit is good or bad or not (or simply designed to trick you) is up for you to decide for yourself.

In the case of a nihilist, they may have recognized that the ruler/yardstick they received in their kit was in the shape of a bendy straw and therefore not useful for them. As they keep digging in their toolboxes, they may decide that all the tools they received are junk or that they simply do not have the patience to go through them all and would rather start with a clean slate as to how they approach the world.

So if a nihilist believes everything the world told to them is a lie, then the onus will be on the nihilist to figure out their own tools as 'truth' or decide that the only 'truth' they need is an empty toolbox.

I would recommend nihilism as the foundation or starting point at which you look at other things. Some nihilists never go beyond the concrete slab of the foundation (and don't want to for various reasons), others rebuild something else. /end Devil's Advocate
